chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, said:

I heard a man saying to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I enter the bathhouse at dawn, and in it are the junub and others besides them. Then I stand and perform ghusl, and some of their water splashes onto me after I have finished.” He said: “Is it not flowing?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “There is no problem.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: the bathhouse or public bathing place
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem

ai.seo_question: Is water splashing from a public bathhouse onto a person during ghusl considered problematic if the water is flowing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of water in a public bathhouse when a person performing ghusl is splashed by water used by others, including those in a state of janabah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that if the water is flowing, there is no problem with it.
